small_guidance:
- Shared memory blew up because the inner `tl.dot(w_vals, tl.trans(x_vals))` with IC_C=64 plus 4 position accumulators (c00..c11) over BLOCK_OC=32×BLOCK_SP=64 is far too large; drop BLOCK_SP to 16 and split the IC dimension into chunks (e.g. IC_BLOCK=16) iterating over IC rather than loading all 64 at once.
- Remove the 4-way (ii,jj) accumulator explosion: process the 2×2 maxpool positions sequentially (one accumulator at a time) or fuse them so only one `[BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP]` tile lives in registers/SMEM at a time.
- Drop `num_stages` to 1 and use `num_warps=4`; consider `tl.dot` with `allow_tf32=True` plus fp16/bf16 weight cast for tile-size headroom.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a two-stage pipeline: (1) a conv+pool+hardtanh kernel that writes the post-pool tile (still fused, but with one program per (N, OC tile, pooled-spatial tile)) using an im2col-style GEMM with BLOCK_M (OC) × BLOCK_N (pooled HW) × BLOCK_K (IC*kh*kw) tiles around 32×32×32; (2) a small reduction kernel that does mean over HW/2×W/2 and tanh. The current "all-in-one" design forces the entire spatial axis through one program, which is why shared memory exploded.
- Alternatively, keep the single-kernel fusion but make it persistent per (N, OC tile): loop over pooled spatial tiles with BLOCK_SP=8 or 16, IC chunked into BLOCK_K=16, and accumulate only a scalar sum per OC across tiles — no 4-way (ii,jj) tiles, instead compute the 4 conv outputs by reusing the same `tl.dot` with shifted x-gathers and reducing immediately to the pool max.
- Since stride=1,pad=1,k=3 makes ConvTranspose2d == Conv2d with flipped weight (already exploited), commit to that and use a standard im2col GEMM template; the maxpool 2× downsample means output is 128×128 — tile pooled-HW with one program per 16×16 pooled tile and one OC tile of 32, which fits SMEM comfortably.
